newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish forest lobby sees output growth at end-97.
newsitem.headline: Finnish forest lobby sees output growth at end-97.

text.p: The forest industry's prospects for 1997 remain unclear and it is difficult to predict when the price of pulp could start to rise, the Finnish Forest Industries Federation said on Tuesday.
But output and exports could increase at the end of the year, it said in a statement.

"There are possibilities for growth in both production and exports of the forest industry at the end of this year," the federation said, adding that so far there were no clear signs of a broad improvement in the industry's market situation.
Production stoppages announced for this spring by North American pulp producers could turn pulp inventories into a decline, the federation said.

"The fall must be considerable before conditions exist for a price rise," it said. "It is difficult to predict when such a level of inventories will be reached that a rise in the price of pulp will be possible," it said.
Cyclical prospects in Europe were expected to improve slightly in 1997 and this was crucial for the Finnish forest industry's exports, the lobby said. @
The output of EU countries was expected to rise 2-2.5 percent this year, it added.
"The dollar's strengthening against EU currencies is a positive factor," it said, noting this was boosting the competitiveness of Europe's exports.
On average, export prices of forest industry products were unlikely to rise, but export revenues were expected to rise due to higher volumes, it said. @
In 1996, the Finnish forest industry's export revenues were 54.1 billion markka, down 5.2 billion or about nine percent on 1995, while the volume of exports fell one percent.

The Finnish forest industry's aggregate 1996 profit after financial items was 5.6 billion markka or about six percent of net sales, compared to the previous year's 12 billion markka (12.3 percent of net sales), the federation said.
The volume of paper exports fell more than seven percent in 1996 on 1995, and export prices fell three percent. @
The average 1996 pulp price was 35 percent lower than in 1995, while prices of sawn goods fell almost 10 percent on average, it said.
The industry's capacity utilisation ratio fell to 85 percent in 1996 from 92 percent in 1995, and production fell almost three percent.
The production of paper fell almost seven percent or by 570,000 tonnes.
"The paper industry has not experienced an output fall of that size since the recession of 1995," the lobby said.
